headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make Continue’s outputs risky to consume alongside the other agent, with prompt-injection and leakage pathways present by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile B can read workspace files and use MCP, while agent A is a content-writing source with broad network egress; if A’s outputs are placed into shared files or MCP-fed content, Continue may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, but the bridge is not guaranteed by A alone, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent A’s generated text is written into a workspace file or MCP payload that agent B reads as prompt content
IF agent B processes file contents without provenance tagging or instruction stripping
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of files B reads automatically
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in B prompts
Disable MCP routes that ingest free-form text
Review any shared workspace for prompt-like content before opening it in B
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to A→B content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B explicitly reads workspace files and editor buffers and can egress broadly; agent A has broad network egress and no data-class limits are listed. If sensitive source code or buffers are present, B can transmit them to its model provider or MCP targets. A is not documented as handling sensitive data, so the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in agent B’s workspace files or editor buffers
IF agent B sends those contents to a remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Use a local model provider for B
Restrict B’s MCP servers to trusted local endpoints
Open only sanitized files in B
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B supports multiple instances with shared state via filesystem and can write files; agent A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent, so concurrent edits or generated artifacts can collide in shared workspace paths. A does not expose write capabilities, so this is not the high-severity same-dir write conflict, but overlapping mutable file use still exists.
conditions: IF agent A’s generated artifacts are saved into the same workspace paths that agent B edits
IF multiple B instances operate on the same filesystem-backed state without locking
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Use per-task worktrees for B
Close duplicate B instances before writing shared files
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on tool calls and editor state, while agent A produces content that B may render or use as context. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors or fabricated content can cascade into code changes or other actions. The profiles show the pathway but not a guaranteed verification failure, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent B uses agent A’s generated text as source material for code or actions
IF B does not independently verify claims before acting on them
mitigations: Require human review of A-generated content before B acts
Ask B to cite file-backed evidence for claims
Limit B to suggestion-only mode for high-impact tasks
Mark A outputs as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for agent A, and agent B only lists model-provider API keys plus workspace data. The pair therefore shows only a weak compliance concern: if regulated data is placed into B’s workspace and then sent to a remote provider, policy mismatch could arise, but the profiles do not prove such data classes exist.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is stored in B’s workspace
IF B routes that data to a non-compliant remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B workspaces
Use a compliant local model for regulated projects
Review provider terms before enabling remote inference
Separate regulated and unregulated projects
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls
